##Trial 1a


```{r load}


library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)

```


```{r 10% sample}

ds <- open_dataset("C:/Users/teger/Downloads/50_data_demo_mds.parquet")

# get row count (streaming, safe)
n <- ds %>% summarise(n = n()) %>% collect() %>% pull(n)

sample_10 <- ds %>%
  head(floor(0.10 * n)) %>%
  collect()
```

```{r collect}


sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%
  select(
    recordId, time, F0, F1, F2, F3, gender, healthCode,
    recordId_demo, recordId_mds,
    `MDS-UPDRS1.1`, `MDS-UPDRS1.3`, `MDS-UPDRS1.4`,
    `MDS-UPDRS1.5`, `MDS-UPDRS1.7`, `MDS-UPDRS1.8`,
    `MDS-UPDRS2.1`, `MDS-UPDRS2.4`, `MDS-UPDRS2.5`,
    `MDS-UPDRS2.6`, `MDS-UPDRS2.7`, `MDS-UPDRS2.8`,
    `MDS-UPDRS2.9`, `MDS-UPDRS2.10`, `MDS-UPDRS2.12`,
    `MDS-UPDRS2.13`
  ) %>%
  collect()
```

```{r rename}

sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%
  mutate(
    MDS_UPDRS1_total = rowSums(
      across(starts_with("MDS-UPDRS1")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    MDS_UPDRS2_total = rowSums(
      across(starts_with("MDS-UPDRS2")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  
  )
```

```{r cleaning}

sample_10 %>%
  select(
    recordId, time, F0, F1, F2, F3, gender, healthCode,
    recordId_demo, recordId_mds, MDS_UPDRS1_total, MDS_UPDRS2_total)

```


```{r sanity filter}
library(mgcv)


sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender),
    severity1 = as.numeric(MDS_UPDRS1_total),
    severity2 = as.numeric(MDS_UPDRS2_total),
    time = as.numeric(time)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(time),
    !is.na(gender),
    !is.na(severity1),
    !is.na(severity2)
  )
```

```{r fit}

library(mgcv)


sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender),
    time_std = as.numeric(scale(time)),
    severity_total = as.numeric(severity_total)
  )

gam_F0 <- gam(
  F0 ~ 
    gender +
    s(time_std, k = 8) +
    s(severity_total, k = 6) +
    ti(time_std, severity_total, k = c(6, 5)) +
    gender:severity_total,
  data   = sample_10,
  method = "REML"
  
)

#did not have enough memory to run this last chunk
```



##Trial 1b

```{r bam replacement for memory efficiency}


features <- c("F0", "F1", "F2", "F3")

bams <- lapply(features, function(f) {
  bam(
    as.formula(paste0(
      f, " ~ s(time_std, k=8) + ",
      "s(severity_total, k=6) + ",
      "ti(time_std, severity_total, k=c(6,5)) + ",
      "gender + gender:severity_total"
    )),
    data = sample_10,
    method = "fREML",
    discrete = TRUE
  )
})

names(bams) <- features

```


```{r prep}


library(mgcv)

sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender),
    time_std = as.numeric(scale(time)),
    severity_total = as.numeric(severity_total)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(F0), !is.na(F1), !is.na(F2), !is.na(F3),
    !is.na(time_std), !is.na(severity_total)
  )

```

```{r}

features <- c("F0", "F1", "F2", "F3")

bams <- lapply(features, function(f) {
  message("Fitting BAM for ", f)
  bam(
    as.formula(paste0(
      f, " ~ ",
      "s(time_std, k=8) + ",                     # time smooth
      "s(severity_total, k=6) + ",              # severity smooth
      "ti(time_std, severity_total, k=c(6,5)) + ", # interaction
      "gender + gender:severity_total"          # gender effects
    )),
    data = sample_10,
    method = "fREML",
    discrete = TRUE
  )
})

names(bams) <- features

```

```{r plotting}

# Base plot for F0 BAM
plot(bams$F0, pages = 1, scheme = 2, rug = FALSE)

# Or ggplot with predict()
library(ggplot2)

# Create prediction grid
pred_data <- expand.grid(
  time_std = seq(min(sample_10$time_std), max(sample_10$time_std), length.out = 100),
  severity_total = mean(sample_10$severity_total, na.rm = TRUE),
  gender = levels(sample_10$gender)
)

preds <- predict(bams$F0, newdata = pred_data, se.fit = TRUE)
pred_data$fit <- preds$fit
pred_data$se <- preds$se.fit

ggplot(pred_data, aes(x = time_std, y = fit, color = gender, fill = gender)) +
  geom_line(size=1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=fit-2*se, ymax=fit+2*se), alpha=0.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title="F0 BAM smooths by gender", x="Time (standardized)", y="F0")

#for this one it didn't generate because it said the graph margins are too large 
```



```{r calculate severity scores}

sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%

    MDS_UPDRS1_total = rowSums(
      across(starts_with("MDS-UPDRS1")),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
```

```{r check}

colnames(sample_10)

```


```{r cleaning}

#removing the MDS columns now that I have the sums for MDS1 and 2

sample_10 %>%
  select(
    recordId, time, F0, F1, F2, F3, gender, healthCode,
    recordId_demo, recordId_mds, MDS_UPDRS1_total, MDS_UPDRS2_total)

```

```{r variable prep}

sample_10 <- sample_10 %>%
  mutate(
    gender = factor(gender),
    time_std = as.numeric(scale(time)),
    severity_total = as.numeric(MDS_UPDRS1_total + MDS_UPDRS2_total)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(F0), !is.na(F1), !is.na(F2), !is.na(F3),
    !is.na(time_std), !is.na(severity_total)
  )
#chatgpt kept telling me it would be easier if i added the severity scores together for now
```

```{r find minimal sample size}
#wanted to find smallest sample size i could take that would still work with running analysis


k_time <- 8
k_severity <- 6
n_gender <- length(unique(sample_10$gender))

# Rule of thumb: 10 * max(k) * n_gender
min_rows <- ceiling(10 * max(k_time, k_severity) * n_gender)
cat("Minimal rows needed:", min_rows, "\n")

```

```{r taking minimal sample by gender}

set.seed(123)
sample_min <- sample_10 %>%
  group_by(gender) %>%
  slice_sample(n = ceiling(min_rows / n_gender)) %>%
  ungroup()

gc()  # free memory
```

```{r fit BAM}
#was advised to use BAM instead of GAM for memory efficiency 
fit_bam <- function(feature, data) {
  bam(
    as.formula(paste0(
      feature, " ~ ",
      "s(time_std, k=", k_time, ") + ",
      "s(severity_total, k=", k_severity, ") + ",
      "ti(time_std, severity_total, k=c(", k_time-2, ",", k_severity-1, ")) + ",
      "gender + gender:severity_total"
    )),
    data = data,
    method = "fREML",
    discrete = TRUE
  )
}

```

```{r F0-3 BAM fit}


features <- c("F0", "F1", "F2", "F3")

bams <- lapply(features, function(f) {
  message("Fitting BAM for ", f)
  fit_bam(f, sample_min)
})
names(bams) <- features

```
```{r BAM plot function}

plot_bam_smooth <- function(bam_model, feature_name, data) {
  pred_data <- expand.grid(
    time_std = seq(min(data$time_std), max(data$time_std), length.out = 100),
    severity_total = mean(data$severity_total),
    gender = levels(data$gender)
  )
  
  preds <- predict(bam_model, newdata = pred_data, se.fit = TRUE)
  pred_data$fit <- preds$fit
  pred_data$se  <- preds$se.fit
  
  ggplot(pred_data, aes(x = time_std, y = fit, color = gender, fill = gender)) +
    geom_line(size=1) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=fit-2*se, ymax=fit+2*se), alpha=0.2, color = NA) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste0(feature_name, " BAM smooths by gender"),
      x = "Time (standardized)",
      y = feature_name
    )
}
```

```{r Plot}

plots <- lapply(features, function(f) plot_bam_smooth(bams[[f]], f, sample_min))

#everything was going good up til here :(


```


Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
